claims.behaviour: The `web-item` `wi-structure-link` (name 'menu:<product>') sits in section `system.top.navigation.bar` with weight 41, label '<product>', tooltip 'Open structure', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` with link id `wi-structure-link`. It is shown only when the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped. It is also the dropdown of Jira's top bar: the sections with location `wi-structure-link` make up its menu, in weight order: welcome (40), recent (50), favorites (60), default (70), query (150), manage (200), processes (250).

It has no condition of its own; it appears with its section.

The `web-item` `wi-default-project-structure` (name 'menu:<product>|Default Project Structure') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-default-structures` with weight 10, label '<abbreviated structure name> - Structure (<project key>)', tooltip 'see this module's tooltip claim', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<structure id>` with link id `wi-default-project-structure`. The structure is the default structure of the project in Jira's current web context. It is shown only when there is such a project, the project is enabled for <product>, its default structure exists and is not archived, differs from the system default structure, and the user can VIEW it. All of that is read for the current user, and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped.

The tooltip of `wi-default-project-structure` is the message '{2} - default structure for project {0}' filled with {0} = the fixed word 'Structure', {1} = the structure name and {2} = the structure description, so it reads '<description> - default structure for project Structure' and never names the project (as the original does).

The `web-panel` `structure-helper-panel` (name 'issue-page:<product> Helper Panel') has location `atl.jira.view.issue.right.context`, weight 1000000 (last in the right column) and label '<product> Helper Panel'. It is shown only when the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped, and `StructureManager.hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser()` is true. It has no visible content: it only hands data to the issue page script.

The helper panel gives the issue page script, per rendering of the issue: the issue id and key; whether to show Structure on this issue; whether the issue is 'unstructured'; whether the panel is auto-collapsed; whether a navigation hint was used; and whether to show time tracking. With no issue in the context the id and key are empty, and show, unstructured and auto-collapsed are false. While the plugin is stopped nothing is filled in, and the script treats all flags as false.

On the issue page 'show Structure' is true only when the issue exists, the user can browse it, its project is enabled for <product> (`getIssueError(issue, false, true)` is null) and `StructureManager.hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser()` is true.

When 'show Structure' is true the panel configuration is computed for the issue page with the issue, its project and the `structure3.navigation.hint` cookie (matched ignoring case on the cookie's name). 'Unstructured' is true when that gives no initial structure or the issue is not in the initial structure (read without an access check). 'Auto-collapsed' is true only when the issue is unstructured and the user's auto-collapse setting is on. 'Navigation hint used' is true when the cookie is not empty, whatever its content and even when Structure is not shown.

The 'show time tracking' value is the dark feature `structure.issuePage.showTimeTracking` (default true), read once when the panel's context provider is created, so changing it needs a plugin restart to take effect.

The `web-panel` `structuremodule` (name 'issue-page:<product> on Issue Page') has location `atl.jira.view.issue.left.context`, weight 899 and label 'Structure'. It is shown only when all hold: the dark feature `structure.feature.showOnIssuePage` is not false (default true); the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped; and `StructureManager.hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser()` is true.

The panel's content must be non-empty for Jira to render the module at all, but it shows nothing: it is one HTML comment. The module stays hidden until `issuePageDecorator` has fitted it out. So a page where the script does not run (or where the issue is not to show Structure) shows no empty Structure section.

The `web-panel` `wp-projectnav-structure` has location `com.almworks.jira.structure:wi-projectnav-structure` and no weight or label. It is shown only when both hold: the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped; and Jira's context holds a project enabled for <product>.

The project page panel requires Jira's issue keyboard shortcuts, the widget's web resources and `wr-project-page`, and shows in this order: the hidden issue operation links; an error message box when the context's error text is not empty (the provider always gives empty text); the hidden project key and id for the script; a toolbar place labelled '<product> toolbar' for assistive technology; and the place of the widget. The issue operation links must come before the widget in the page, for the reason in `ww-structure` (see the claim on issue operation links).

The project panel also carries a scope name, Jira's word for project followed by ': ' and the project's name ('Project: <name>'), and a scope JQL that is never filled in. Nothing reads either one on the client, so they have no visible effect.
With no project object in the panel's context, its context provider logs a warning and answers an empty context.

`gadget-resources` is a dependency-only web-resource: Jira's global, static, fields, set-focus and throbber resources, the small AUI spinner, the gadget publisher's scripts, Jira's common gadget resources, `widget`, `gadget-bare` and Jira's English calendar. The gadget page needs all of them before its start-up script runs.

`cfd-gadget-resources` is a dependency-only web-resource: as `gadget-resources` but with Jira's field templates, the AUI date picker and Jira's light common gadget resources instead of the full one, plus `widget`, `c3` and `cfd-gadget-bare`. The gadget's page requires Jira's English calendar separately.

`macro-resources` gives the external gadget page the widget (`widget`), the visibility helper (`visibility-observer`), the gadget's view-link and transform helpers (shared with `gadget-bare`) and the gadget stylesheet. It contains no gadget framework, because the page is a plain Jira page.

On Jira 9.12 the web-resource `adjustIssuePage` (name 'web-resource:Issue Page Resources for Jira 9', restricted to Jira [9.0.0,10.0.0)) is bound to context `jira.view.issue`, depends on `widget-atlas-deps` and `adjustIssuePageCond`, and is delivered only when the dark feature `structure.feature.showOnIssuePage` is not false (default true). The check takes part in the resource URL as a URL-reading condition, so the answer is cached with the batch. A second declaration with the same key covers Jira 10 and later.

On Jira 9.12 the web-resource `adjustIssuePageCond` (name 'web-resource:Issue Page Decorator for Jira 9', restricted to Jira [9.0.0,10.0.0)) depends on `issuePageDecorator` and is delivered only when the current user may use <product>. The condition is URL-reading: a user who may not use <product> gets a resource URL with `s_disabled=y` and no script. A second declaration with the same key covers Jira 10 and later.

`structure-projectnav-css` is stylesheet only: the icons of the <product> sidebar entry and of the Agile tab. It depends on `fonts` and is bound to contexts `jira.browse.project`, `jira.admin`, `gh-rapid`, `gh-rapid-plan` and `gh-rapid-work`. It has no behaviour.

`visibility-observer` watches the widget's container in a gadget or macro. The first time at least 1% of it (or a given threshold) enters the viewport, the widget's caches are cleared and its layout forced, then an optional callback runs; after that it stops watching, even if the callback fails (the failure is logged as a warning). This exists because a widget laid out while hidden, such as inside a collapsed expand macro, has no size. With no container on the page it logs a warning and does nothing.

When the document is ready, on a page where the issue page script is loaded, it starts unless a structure widget's place already exists on the page (as on the <product> Board's issue details), in which case it does nothing at all. On start it declares the page as the `issue` page (the value sent as `forPage`) and marks the page as the issue page for styling.

The script reads the helper panel's data (`structure-helper-panel`) at start, and again each time Jira fires its issue-refreshed event, even when nothing changed. On a Jira without that event it re-reads on Jira's new-content event for the page load and for a refresh of the helper panel only. With no helper panel the issue id is 0, Structure and time tracking are off, 'unstructured' and 'auto-collapsed' count as true, and the panel is noted as missing.

For each distinct issue id, the script sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui?forIssue=<issue id>` once, and shares the answer with the section, the settings dialog and time tracking. Showing the same issue again sends no new request. Issue id 0 sends nothing. A failed request only logs a warning: the settings button stays hidden and no structure is opened.

After the `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` for an issue finishes (success or failure), the script clears the `structure3.navigation.hint` cookie and keeps its value in memory. Before a settings `POST` for an issue it puts that value back, and clears it again when the POST finishes, so that the POST's recomputed configuration sees the same hint.

When the issue shows Structure and Jira's Structure module is on the page, the script fits it out once: it replaces the module's operations with one settings button, adds a place for the 'not in structure' warning to the header and a widget place to the content, swaps the module for this version and makes it visible. Without Jira's module on the page it logs a warning and does nothing.
When the issue must not show Structure, the section is taken off the page (kept in memory), and any widget errors on display are dismissed.

When Jira redraws the issue and drops the section, while the new issue shows Structure, the same section, with its widget and its state, replaces the new module. If the widget exists, it is anchored and pinned on the new issue, focuses it initially, re-binds its mouse handling and help panels, lays itself out, and Jira's new-content event fires with the reason `structureSectionReinserted`; a failure of that event only logs a warning. The settings button is shown and rebound to the kept dialog.

The section header's warning reads '(does not include <issue key>)' with the tooltip 'The currently viewed issue is not in the selected structure'. The key is refreshed each time the section is placed on a page.

The warning is shown when the widget's primary panel has reported that the issue has no rows in the open structure. Until the widget reports (including when no widget exists yet) it is shown when the issue page's 'unstructured' flag is true and Structure is on. Once the widget has reported, the report decides; a report of 'not known' (null) goes back to the flag.

After each new reading of the page data with a real issue, the section is set collapsed when Jira's own remembered collapsed state lists this module, or when the issue is unstructured and auto-collapsed and no navigation hint was used; otherwise it is expanded. Example: an issue not in the structure with auto-collapse on starts collapsed, unless the user came to it from a structure grid.
10 ms after a click on the section's toggle in its header the section's expanded state is read again. Off the page it counts as not known.

The widget is created the first time the section is expanded, not before; a collapsed section sends none of the widget's requests. When expanded again it only lays itself out. Its options: height follows the grid's content, at most 15 rows, and the panel can be hidden.

On creation the widget is anchored on the page's issue: it pins that issue and focuses it initially. When the URL fragment is a positive number, that row is focused initially and the fragment is cleared (`#1234`).
Errors of the section's widget are displayed only while the page's issue id is positive and the issue shows Structure; otherwise an error is dismissed without display.
The widget opens `initialStructure.id` of the panel configuration, whenever that value becomes a positive id. The single-structure mode follows `singleStructure` of the configuration.

On creation of the section's widget, footers become responsive and the structure info dialog is available. While the user drags Jira's split-view divider (in the issue navigator) the widget lays itself out 100 ms after the drag events stop, when the section is on the page.

The section's title depends on the open structure (or, before one is open, `initialStructure`) and on the expanded state. Collapsed, with more than one structure available and a known name: 'Structure: <abbreviated name>', tooltip the description. Expanded, or in single-structure mode: 'Structure', tooltip '<abbreviated name> - <description>' (no ' - ' with no description). With no name: 'Structure' with no tooltip. Names are abbreviated to 40 characters. With no configuration or an unknown expanded state the title is not touched.

When an edit made in the section's widget finishes uploading successfully, and the changed item is an issue that is the page's issue, or appears in Jira's issue links module, or in Jira's sub-task list, the script fires Jira's refresh-issue-page event for the page's issue. Other edits leave the issue page alone. A failure logs a warning.

A Jira issue dialog opened from a row of the section acts on that row's issue, not the page's issue, by making Jira's 'current issue id' answer the id on the dialog's trigger while such a dialog is current. After it, Jira's sub-task refresh runs only when that id is the page's issue. When Jira's labels dialog is opened from a row of another issue, Jira is given nothing to update, so the page issue's labels on display stay untouched.
When Jira announces new content for the module `structuremodule`, the script fires Jira's lock-panel-refreshing event for it, so that Jira's panel refresh does not replace the section.
On Internet Explorer only, the section is detached before Jira's issue viewer redraws an issue on initialization. Jira 9.12 does not support that browser, so a rebuild may leave this out.

The <product> time tracking section is loaded with `GET /secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa?decorator=none&structureId=<open structure>&issueId=<page issue>`, always with Jira's cache-busting parameter, as HTML. It needs: 'show time tracking' on, an open or initial structure, and an issue. It is sent when one of these changes, when Jira refreshes its time tracking module, and after a poll that reports changes. A request with the same parameters while one is under way is not repeated, and a change of parameters drops the older answer.

When the answer to the time tracking request carries a job id instead of data, the script waits and asks `GET /secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa?decorator=none&jobId=<id>`. The waits come from the shared async back-off list, default 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 15000, 30000, 60000 ms, the last one repeating. An answer that carries the back-off override replaces that list for the page. Each poll is skipped if a newer request has started.

When a time tracking request fails, or the page got no reply, a warning is logged and whichever section exists is shown: the Structure one when present, else Jira's. No error message is displayed. The next trigger may send the same request again.

An answer with no section (empty fragment) when none is on the page yet leaves Jira's time tracking module on display. With a Structure section already on the page, it stays, structure data then counts as absent, and the section takes the state for that case (Jira data only, or hidden).

The <product> time tracking section is placed in the right column after Jira's time tracking module, else after Jira's dates module, else after Jira's people module, else at the column's end. Jira's own module is hidden while it is shown. The collapsed state starts from Jira's remembered collapsed state for this section's module.
In the <product> time tracking table, each term of the data list gets the prefix 'Σ' and a no-break space, after trimming: 'Estimated' becomes 'Σ Estimated'.

The <product> time tracking section has four states. No structure data and no Jira data: the section is hidden. No structure data but Jira data: Jira's data with no checkbox. <product> data and the checkbox 'Include structure sub-issues' off: the checkbox and Jira's data. <product> data and the checkbox on: the checkbox and the aggregated structure data.

The checkbox 'Include structure sub-issues' (tooltip 'Calculate aggregate estimates and time spent that include sub-issues of this issue in the selected structure') starts on, unless the user turned it off earlier. The choice is remembered in the browser across issues and visits, for all structures, by a text 'true' or 'false'. A change only switches the display; no request is sent.

With no time tracking data of Jira's own the non-aggregated part shows 'This issue does not have its own time tracking information.'. With Jira's data it shows a copy of what Jira's module holds, and a 'include sub-tasks' checkbox in that copy keeps working: it switches between single and aggregate figures.

The section's Log Work link (`/secure/CreateWorklog!default.jspa?id=<issue id>`, Jira's title and text) appears when the server says so. When a new answer with structure data updates an existing section, the link's target comes from the answer; otherwise from Jira's module. With no target it stays as it is.
While the widget exists, a poll answer with a non-empty change of any forest or of the items list triggers a reload of the time tracking section. An empty poll answer does not.

When Jira announces a refresh of its time tracking module (panel-refreshed or new-content for that module) and parameters are known, Jira's module is hidden again if the Structure section exists, and the Structure section reloads; a failure logs a warning.

When the page's data says Structure is off (and the helper panel is present), the <product> time tracking section is hidden and Jira's module is shown. When 'show time tracking' is off, requests stop and an answer on its way is dropped; turning it on loads the section.
After updating the section, the script fires Jira's new-content event for it with the reason `timeTrackingPanelUpdatedByStructure`, so that Jira binds its controls. A failure logs a warning.

The issue section's settings button (tooltip '<product> on the Issue Page Settings') stays hidden until the settings have loaded from the configuration, then shows and opens the settings dialog '<product> Settings'. Its dialog is built on first opening.

The issue settings dialog holds, in order: 'Auto-switch to:' (checkbox); radio 'Structure with the displayed issue'; radio 'Default structure: <abbreviated default name, or ?>'; 'Keep structure selection when navigating to another issue' (checkbox); 'Auto-minimize panel when issue is not in structure' (checkbox). Below them: a link to the plugin's documentation on panel settings, reading 'Help' with the title 'Open documentation on <product> panel settings' (the implementer's own link), and the button 'Close'. In single-structure mode only the last checkbox is shown.

The auto-switch controls map to the value `autoSwitch`: checkbox off gives `off`; on with the default radio gives `default`; on with the other radio gives `withIssue`. From the server's value: `default` or `withIssue` checks the box and that radio; `off` unchecks the box and leaves both radios unchecked as a value. Example: checking the box with no radio checked gives `withIssue`. Each click, key press or change is evaluated.

When `userConfigurable` is false (anonymous users), every input in the settings dialog is disabled and labels look disabled. The two radios are also disabled when auto-switch is off: they are enabled only with `userConfigurable` true and the value `default` or `withIssue`.

The settings dialog of the issue and project pages is an inline dialog 460 wide, offset -360 from its trigger, that closes on a second click of the trigger and hides by itself after a delay of 20 seconds (Jira's inline dialog option `hideDelay`). Clicks in it do not close it. 'Close' hides it. Its content is built once and kept.
The settings dialog shows the configuration's `defaultStructure` name, abbreviated to 40 characters, or '?' with no default.

While a settings upload runs, a small spinner is visible in the dialog; its state changes at most every 500 ms. When an upload fails, the dialog shows 'Failed to upload settings' and re-fits itself; the message goes away when the next upload starts.

The dialog's settings are three values read from the configuration: `autoSwitch` (default `off` when absent), `autoCollapse` (default true) and `keepStructureWhenNavigating` (default true). Every new configuration replaces them without sending anything.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` is sent once per page context: with `forIssue`, or else `forAgileBoard`, or else `forProject` = the project key (first one given); and `preferredStructure` when one is given. A failure logs a warning only. An empty answer leaves the state unchanged.

A change of a setting by the user sends `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`, JSON, with only the changed keys plus the context parameter of the page (`forIssue`, `forAgileBoard` or `forProject`). There is no debounce: each change gives one POST. The answer replaces the configuration only if no other upload is still in progress. Failure sets the upload error, logs a warning, and the dialog keeps the user's value.

On all three pages a positive `initialStructure.id` in the configuration opens that structure in the widget, including a later change of it. On the issue page and the Agile tab, `singleStructure` true switches the widget to single-structure mode; on false it switches back. The project page has no single-structure mode.

On Agile boards the tab's script installs itself when the document is ready, and acts only when the tab's link is clicked or Jira Software fires `GH.DetailView.updated` while the tab's content is visible. Until then, it makes no requests. With Jira Software absent it is not loaded at all.

On first opening, the tab reads the issue id of the board's detail view and the board id, marks the page as the Agile tab with that board id, and creates the widget. Inside a detail section the widget's height follows the model and selectors with at most 15 rows; otherwise it fills its container. The widget can be hidden and uses the Agile Board View, the view id -3 ('Agile Board View').

The tab sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` once, on first opening, with `preferredStructure=<remembered id>` when one is remembered. When the detail view has an issue the context is only `forIssue=<that issue>`, and `forAgileBoard` is not sent, so the server treats it as an issue page and the project's enablement counts (see `rest-v1`). `forAgileBoard=<board id>` goes only with no issue. Later issues send no new request. As with any `forIssue` GET, the `structure3.navigation.hint` cookie is cleared when it finishes. A failure logs a warning: no structure opens by itself.

The structure last opened in the tab is remembered per board id in the browser. A change to a positive id that differs from the remembered id updates it. This is the `preferredStructure` of the next opening.

The pin state is remembered in the browser, for all boards together, and starts on unless it was turned off. It changes when the panel's pin changes: a pin means on, no pin means off. On each new issue, the widget anchors on it; with the pin on, the issue is pinned; with the pin off it is focused initially instead.

When the board's detail view shows another issue (`GH.DetailView.updated` with the tab visible), the widget is anchored on the new issue 300 ms later, the info dialog and help panels are revived and the layout forced. If Jira Software emptied the tab, the kept tab content goes back in first. Several updates within 300 ms give one reaction.
When an edit in the tab's widget finishes uploading successfully, the script fires `GH.RapidBoard.causeBoardReload`, so the board reloads. A failed edit does not.

The tab's widget lays itself out on window scroll; on window resize at once when the backlog is visible, otherwise 300 ms after the last resize unless Jira Software gave a delayed-resize event, which is used instead with no extra delay; and 300 ms after Jira Software's backlog width check or detail width store.
Errors of the tab's widget are never displayed: they are dismissed. Footers are responsive and the info dialog is available.

The project page script needs the hidden project key and id in the panel. With either one missing it logs a warning and does nothing. When both are there it declares the page as the `project` page (the value sent as `forPage`) and starts when the document is ready.

The page uses the first heading before the board place, else the first heading of the page's header, and otherwise adds a heading 'Structure'. The settings control goes before that heading. The board is extended over its container's padding so that it fills the page panel.

The project page's widget fills the window with at least 6 rows, does not expand anchors, can be hidden and shows issue details. It always uses one panel: the two-panel mode is excluded on this page. An issue row in the URL fragment (`#1234`, a positive number) is focused initially and the fragment cleared.
The script sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui?forProject=<project key>` once. The widget opens `initialStructure.id` as soon as that arrives, and the info dialog is available.
The settings button with the tooltip '<product> on the Project Page Settings' stays hidden until the settings have loaded, then it shows and opens the dialog '<product> Settings'.

The project settings dialog has one checkbox 'Auto-switch to default structure: <abbreviated default name, or ?>', the upload message and spinner of `pageCommons`, and 'Close'. Checked sends `autoSwitch`=`default`, unchecked `off`; a stored `withIssue` shows unchecked. With `userConfigurable` false the checkbox is disabled.

The project settings dialog's link 'Change default structure' is shown only when the configuration's `projectAdmin` is true, and opens `/secure/StructureProjectSettings.jspa?projectKey=<URL-encoded key>`.
When Jira's project sidebar finishes collapsing or expanding, the widget lays itself out again; an error is ignored. With no sidebar nothing is bound.
When Jira's page parameter for the logged-in user differs from Jira's actual logged-in user, the page corrects the hidden parameter, so that later scripts see the right user.

The `gadget` `structure-gadget` (name 'gadget:<product>', location `gadgets/structure-gadget.xml`) has the title and directory title 'Structure', the description 'Displays issue structure and lets you edit the hierarchy and the issues.', category JIRA, `scrolling` false, height 300, and works in the views `default` and `canvas`. It requires the gadget features setprefs, settitle, minimessage, dynamic-height, views and oauthpopup, and optionally gadget-directory and `atlassian.util`. Its messages come from `gadget.common` and `s.g`.

The <product> gadget's hidden preferences, whose names are stored by Jira's dashboard and are read by `dashboard-gadget-data-exporter`: `structureId`, `viewId`, `filterId`, `customTitle`, `numRows` (default 10), `isConfigured` (default false), `allowChanges` (default true), `useCanvasSettings` (default false), `canvas-viewId`, `canvas-numRows`, `filterType`, `filterQuery`.

The <product> gadget's page requires `gadget-resources`, `com.atlassian.teams:teams-wr-custom-field-styles-common`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-view-issue` and the resource context `structure.widget` (so companion apps' parts load), then starts the gadget with the Jira base URL. A required resource of an app that is absent adds nothing, and the gadget works without it.

The gadget compares Jira's renderer base URL with the gadget's base URL: equal means `local` mode; different, or no renderer URL function, means `remote` mode (shown on another application). In both modes all requests go to the gadget's base URL.

In `remote` mode, before anything else the gadget asks the host application `GET /rest/api/user/current` (a Confluence REST call). An answer with `type` = `anonymous` means an anonymous viewer; any failure logs a warning and counts as not anonymous. With no Confluence the call fails and start-up goes on.

In `remote` mode for a non-anonymous viewer, the gadget first calls Jira's `GET /rest/gadget/1.0/currentUser`, then the configs. If this stub call fails, a warning is logged and the gadget never starts. Anonymous and `local` viewers skip it.

The gadget fetches `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/widgetConfigs` once before it starts. With a failed request it starts with built-in values. Values used: `local` or `remote` by the mode, each with `pollInterval` (default 15000), `minCachedRows` (default 20), `preloadRowsFactor` (default 2), and `allowNodeWandering`; a non-empty `retryBackoff` replaces the retry delays (default 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 ms).
On start the gadget also asks Jira's `GET /rest/api/2/serverInfo`, and notes `version` from the answer on the page for version-specific styles. Nothing else depends on it.
The gadget is created through Jira's gadget framework with the OAuth check `/rest/gadget/1.0/currentUser`, a view and a config form.

Row limit: a value from 2 to 50 is taken, anything else gives 10. The limit is `numRows`, except that, when `useCanvasSettings` is `true` and the gadget is maximized, `canvas-numRows` is used if not empty. View: `viewId`, except that, under the same two conditions, a positive `canvas-viewId` replaces it. No view means the fallback view -1.

The gadget's widget has: height following the model and selectors; at least 2 rows; at most the row limit; poll interval from the configs (default 15000 ms); no user-inactivity threshold (0); `minCachedRows` = the larger of the configured value (default 20) and the row limit times the preload factor (default 2). Example: row limit 15 and defaults give 30.
The gadget's widget is forced read-only in `remote` mode, and whenever `allowChanges` is not `true`.

When `isConfigured` is `true`, the gadget sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta` with `structureId`, `viewId`, `canvasViewId` and `filterId` (the number after `filter-`, 0 when none), all as whole numbers. The structure opens only after a good answer. When the gadget is not configured there is no request and no structure.

On the gadget's meta answer: a failed request or an empty answer shows 'Sorry, <product> gadget is not available.'; a first entry in `errors.errorMessages` shows that message's text, with the structure id as parameter (`s.g.no-such-structure` reads 'Sorry, structure with ID <id> does not exist or you don't have permissions to view it.'); an answer with no `structure` shows that same 'no such structure' text. In these cases no structure opens.

On a good meta answer: the error is removed; the title is set; the view choices for the form are kept from `view` and `canvasView` (abbreviated to 40 characters); `view.writable` decides whether the view may be saved (no `view` means not); and `loggedInUser` sets Jira's `remote-user` and `remote-user-fullname` page values, when given.

The gadget's title is `customTitle` after unescaping and URL-decoding when not empty, else 'Structure: <name abbreviated to 40 characters>'. Printing the page shows that title in place of the grid's heading text; before it is known the print text is 'Structure'.

Filter preferences are read as: `filterQuery` unescaped and URL-decoded; `filterId` of the form `filter-<id>`, 0 when absent or not a number; `filterType` as stored, but when it is empty it counts as `saved` with an id and `none` without.

A gadget's filter becomes a query-filter transformation of the panel: `none` or no type gives none; `saved` with an id gives the JQL `filter="<filter name, or id when the name is unknown>"`; `text`, `jql` or `sjql` with a non-empty query gives that query with that type; anything else gives none. With a transformation, the panel opens `{structureId, transforms:[...]}`, otherwise just the id. A structure id of 0 or less opens nothing.
The saved filter's name comes from the meta answer's `filter.name`; when it is absent, the id is used instead.

When the gadget's meta answer has a non-empty `operations` list and the page has no operation links yet, one hidden link per operation is added, with the id, style class and URL given; the grid's issue actions use them.

The gadget uses the framework's footer as the widget's footer: the board link, row statistics, progress, undo and redo, warnings and background-process parts move there, and replace any earlier ones. The footer is responsive. No licence warning ever appears there.

After any change of the widget's height, 50 ms after a change of the panel's root paths, and after the form changes, the gadget resizes its frame to fit. The height is the header and footer plus the grid's height, or the error's height when unavailable. Jira's system messages are added; with the config form open, its height is added as well. While the form is open a window resize also refits, at most every 100 ms.
When the gadget's container first becomes visible (see `visibility-observer`), the header and footer heights are measured afresh, and the gadget resizes.

While the config form is shown the widget's keyboard is off. On returning to the view without a change, the keyboard is back on; after a change of structure, view or filter in the form, the view is redrawn instead (the framework is told to refresh).

The gadget's config form has, in order: error list; 'Structure' (required); 'View' (required); 'Filter Type'; 'Query'; 'Filter' (only when Jira's filter picker exists); 'Title'; 'Visible Rows'; the checkbox 'Allow changes (subject to permissions)' (not in `remote` mode); the checkbox 'Alternative settings when maximized'; a second 'View'; and a second 'Visible Rows'. The form is sent to `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate` by the framework. Its fields' names are the parameters of that call. On success the framework stores them as preferences, including `isConfigured`.
A small spinner shows above the form when requests have been running for 500 ms; it follows local requests and those of the gadget's script.

The 'Structure' picker is a single select with a dropdown button, filled from `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures?query=<typed text>`; it starts on the current structure's abbreviated name. A first request goes with an empty query when opened; a typed query needs 1 character. An invalid entry reverts to the last value. The answer's `errorMessages` go to the form's error list, and a chosen structure (id above 0) clears its field error. The chosen id is sent as `structureId`.
Choosing a structure in the form does not change the widget behind the form. The form's choice is not connected to the preview, so the new structure shows only after saving (as the original does).

The 'View' picker works like the 'Structure' picker with `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views?structureId=0&query=<typed text>`: the chosen structure is not passed on, so `structureId` is always 0 and the suggestions come from the global default menu (as the original does). A chosen view is applied to the widget at once (when the field fits the mode) and its error cleared. The second 'View' has the name `canvas-viewId`.

Choosing a view previews it in the widget only for the field of the current mode: with 'Alternative settings when maximized' on and the gadget maximized the second field; otherwise the first. In the normal view mode, the second field never previews.

'Filter Type' offers: 'No filter' (`none`), 'Text' (`text`), 'JQL' (`jql`), 'S-JQL' (`sjql`), 'Saved filter' (`saved`). The field 'Query' (required) shows only for Text, JQL and S-JQL. The saved 'Filter' field shows only for Saved filter; leaving that type clears the chosen filter.

The Query text is sent URL-encoded in the hidden field `filterQuery`. JQL autocompletion is on only for the type JQL, using Jira's search data (`/secure/StructureSearchData.jspa`, see `ww-structure`).

For the types JQL and S-JQL with a non-empty query, 1000 ms after the last typing, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/query/validate?type=<type>&q=<query>` is sent. An answer without errors shows the good mark; `errors` in the answer, or a failure, shows the bad mark. A good answer for an older query is ignored. Text queries and other types make no request and clear the mark. A valid filter is not applied to the widget until the form is saved, because the form's structure choice is not connected to the preview (as the original does).
When the form's filter gives no transformation (no filter, empty query), the panel's transformations are removed at once.

'Filter' uses Jira's filter picker. A 'clear' link next to it empties the choice and restores Jira's 'no filter selected' text. The script watches the hidden id every 100 ms while the field is visible, since the picker gives no change event, and stops once it is hidden.

'Title' starts with the decoded custom title. The hidden `customTitle` value is the trimmed text, URL-encoded, and is empty when the text is blank, which leaves the title automatic. The structure's name never fills the field, nor is compared to it, because the form's choice is not passed on (as the original does).

'Visible Rows' (description 'Maximum number of visible rows (up to 50).') starts at the stored value when valid (2 to 50), else 10. Typing another value out of that range, or no number, puts the last good value back on change. The second field has the name `canvas-numRows`.

'Alternative settings when maximized' starts from `useCanvasSettings`, and shows or hides the second 'View' and 'Visible Rows'. In the maximized view, changing it also re-applies the view of the current mode.
'Allow changes (subject to permissions)' starts checked when `allowChanges` is `true`; the checkbox's value is `true`.

The button 'New View...' (title 'Create a new view based on the current view configuration') shows only when the user may create views, as `loadJiraConfig` says, and is enabled only when the current view has columns. It toggles a line with 'View Name', a text field, the button 'Create View' and the link 'Cancel'. On opening the name is 'View for Gadget #<gadget id>' (0 when unknown), selected and focused.

'Create View' is enabled when the name is non-blank, views can be created, the view has columns and no save runs. It saves the current view under that name, through the view model (see `rest-v2` views). On success the line closes, and the new view becomes the 'View' selection, abbreviated, with the description as title. Enter in the name field acts as 'Create View', Escape as 'Cancel'.

When the chosen view has an id above 0 and is not shared with everyone, a notice shows: 'This view is not public. If a user looking at this gadget does not have access to this view, a default view is used instead.'. The link 'Let everyone use this view' (title 'Share this view with everyone') shows only when the user may share views and may administer the view; it shares it through the widget's action `view.share-all`.
Required fields get a required mark after the label. Its hidden text is the unresolved key `{s.g.config.required}`, not 'required parameter' (as the original does).

Each form field has one error place, named `<field id>-error`, which the framework fills after validation. Fields with a check clear it when the value turns good: a structure id above 0; an attribute spec that is empty, `{}` or has an `id`.
The error list at the top of the form is hidden while empty. It lists messages from picker answers, slides open when one arrives, and closes and empties when there are none.

Under the gadget's widget, when the view is adjusted, the footer shows 'View has been adjusted.' and the link 'Revert' (title 'Revert to the view configuration saved on the server'). It reverts the view through the widget. The earlier copy of this line, if any, is replaced.

When the user may configure the gadget and the view is writable, a link 'Save' (title 'Save changes to the view on the server') and a separator '|' show before 'Revert'. With a small footer the text is 'Save View'. A click saves the current view when it is adjusted. When saving fails, an error flag shows the message and closes by itself, and from then on the save text is empty and the revert link reads 'Revert View', as it does whenever the view is not writable. The texts change only on a change of those states.
While saving a view a small spinner shows in the line, only while requests run too. Saving ends when the save answers, the view stops being adjusted, or requests stop.

In a gadget, loading indicators of the framework are off; cookies go through the gadget's own cookie functions; the dirty-form warning is off; and popups from inside the frame are placed in the top window on WebKit and Mozilla browsers, with mouse tracking over both windows. A failure to adapt the popups logs a warning only.
Jira's throbber works only in `local` mode; elsewhere it is a no-op.

In `remote` mode requests go one at a time, in order; the next starts when the previous completes. Each caller's success or error then runs, with the answer's promise. In `local` mode they go directly.
In `remote` mode, Jira's calls carry `Accept: application/json, text/javascript, */*; q=0.01` and `Content-Type` of the call, default `application/json; charset=UTF-8`.
A request to a URL ending in `.jspa` is made as HTML, even when the gadget's default type is JSON; the default then returns to JSON. Each success, error and complete callback runs once.

In `remote` mode on Data Center, the answers to poll and subscription calls carry the cookie `X-Structure-DC-Meta` = `<node id>|<retry count>`. The first node seen, with its count (default 1), is remembered. An answer from the same node resets the number of misses allowed to that count.

An answer from another node is dropped, not given to the caller: while misses remain the request is retried. When they run out, a warning is logged. If `allowNodeWandering` is on, the node is forgotten, the subscriptions are re-created and a poll is requested. If it is off, requests stop and the error 'Problem downloading updates from the server.' is shown with a description that says the originator node cannot be reached and updates are stopped.
In `remote` mode, and only there, the gadget registers a core extension with the key `com.almworks.jira.structure:remote-gadget-extension`, the client side of `remote-gadget-extension`.

After a request to re-subscribe, regular polling and subscription uploads are blocked, and the poll the gadget asks for directly is the one that goes out. In it the extension sends one window per subscription that has a forest spec and rows: `forestSpec`, `rowIndexes` (positions of the rows in the local forest), `attributes`, `oldBackendId`. With none the extension sends nothing. Before that poll's answer is processed, its `subscriptionUpdates` are dropped.

When a poll answer holds the extension's data, each subscription with a mapped id gets the new id, and its values and rows are taken from the answer, its pending state cleared. Whatever the outcome, the block ends with that answer, and a failure is logged as an error.
The extension keeps a forest subscription for each forest spec in use, added when a subscription starts or changes and dropped when it closes, so that the row positions can be computed at any time.

The `gadget` `cfd-gadget` (name 'gadget:Cumulative Flow Diagram', location `gadgets/cfd/cfd-gadget.xml`) has the title 'Predictive Cumulative Flow Diagram', category Charts, `scrolling` false, height 500, and the views `default` and `canvas`, and requires the same gadget features as `structure-gadget`, with messages from `gadget.common` and `s.cfd`. Its directory description states that it runs a per-team completion simulation and shows a cumulative flow chart reaching into the future, about one sentence and marked experimental; the vendor contact in the original's text is left out.

The CFD gadget's hidden preferences: `scopeStructureId`, `trainingStructureId`, `trainingPeriod` (default -1), `estimationIssueTypes`, `scopeIssueTypes`, `teamAttributeSpec`, `targetDate`, `whenAppearedAttributeSpec`, `whenWorkStartedAttributeSpec`, `whenCompletedAttributeSpec`, `ignoreThreshold`, `adjustments`, `customTitle` (never used), `isConfigured` (default false).
The CFD gadget's page requires `cfd-gadget-resources` and `jira.webresources:calendar-en`, then starts with the Jira base URL.

On start the CFD gadget sends `GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/status` once. `enabled` true starts it. A false answer or a failed request shows the disabled message. With no answer within 5 seconds, it starts as if enabled.

When the feature is off, the CFD gadget shows only a message of about three sentences: what the predictions feature does, and links to the plugin's documentation (the implementer's own links; the vendor's are left out). There is no form or chart.
When one of Jira's anonymous-access events (`ajax.anonymousAccessDenied`, `ajax.anonymousAccess`) has fired by the time the gadget would start, it does not start: it shows nothing.

The CFD gadget fetches the widget configs like `gadget-bare`, only as a start signal: their values are not used. Then it starts through Jira's gadget framework with the OAuth check `/rest/gadget/1.0/currentUser`.

The CFD gadget's screen holds, top down: a centered 'Loading...' spinner; the error; the result (left the chart with its title and 'Trending' date; right the 'Metrics' table with its date); the tools links 'Trace' and 'Refresh'; and a hidden read-only trace box.

With `isConfigured` not `true` the gadget shows 'PCFD Gadget is not configured. Please click "..." and select "Edit" to set the configuration.' under the 'Loading...' text, which stays (as the original does). No request is sent, and 'Refresh' does nothing.

Attribute preferences are JSON, escaped by the framework. When absent or unreadable the defaults are: team `{"id":"project","format":"text"}`; when added `{"id":"created","format":"time"}`; work started `{"id":"transition-date","params":{"transition":"first","category":"indeterminate"},"format":"time"}`; completed `{"id":"transition-date","params":{"transition":"latest","category":"done"},"format":"time"}`; adjustments `{}`.
List preferences split on `,` or `|` and drop blank entries; an empty preference gives an empty list. Example: `1|2,,3` gives 1, 2, 3.
The `adjustments` preference is a JSON object, HTML-escaped and URL-encoded, keyed by team name, each value `{throughput, predictedStories}`. It is unescaped, decoded and HTML-unescaped to read it.

When configured, the gadget sends `POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta`, JSON, with all settings: `scopeStructureId`, `trainingStructureId`, `trainingPeriod`, `estimationIssueTypes`, `scopeIssueTypes`, `teamAttributeSpec`, `targetDate`, `whenAppearedAttributeSpec`, `whenWorkStartedAttributeSpec`, `whenCompletedAttributeSpec`, `ignoreThreshold`, `adjustments`. A failed request shows 'PCFD Gadget Unavailable', and the 'Loading...' text stays.

With an empty meta answer the error 'PCFD Gadget Unavailable' shows; with a non-empty `errors.errorMessages` the first message shows as it is. In both, the spinner and tools are hidden. Field errors alone do not stop it: only general messages count. On success the title is set, `loggedInUser` sets Jira's `remote-user` values, and the structures are kept for the form.
The title is 'Predictive Cumulative Flow Diagram for <scope name abbreviated to 40 characters>', or 'Predictive Cumulative Flow Diagram' with no scope structure.

After a good meta answer, and on Refresh, the gadget sends `POST /rest/cfd/1.0/simulation/cfd`, JSON: `scopeStructureId`, `trainingStructureId`; `config` with the two issue type lists, `teamAttributeSpec`, `targetDate`, the three time attributes and `trainingPeriod`; `simulations` 50; `ignoreThreshold`; and `adjustments`. On Refresh, `adjustments` are read anew from the preference.
On a failed simulation the spinner goes, the result is cleared and the error reads 'PCFD Simulation Problem: <detail>'. The detail is `message` of a JSON answer, else the answer's text, else '???'.

A result counts as valid when `overallChart.timestamps` has more than one entry, or `teamStats` is not empty. An invalid result shows 'There is no data to show. Please check the gadget settings and the content of the selected structures. Make sure there are completed Delivery items and epics.'. The chart is drawn only with more than one time point, and the table only with teams.

The chart's title is the scope structure's name, or '<?>'. The 'Trending' date is `completion.mean`. The table's header shows 'Target Date' and the target date when `deliveryTargetDate` is set, otherwise 'Trending' and the completion date. Both dates and the chart get the problem mark when any team has a prediction problem or misses a positive target date.
A team has a problem when it has `predictionProblem`, or when a positive target date exists and its `completion.mean` is later than that date.
Dates show as `YYYY-MM-DD` in the browser's time zone. A missing date or a value below 86400000 ms shows '?'.

Throughput shows rounded to 1 decimal: 2.345 shows 2.3. Counts show as whole numbers. Adjustments show with a sign when positive and with '%': 10 shows +10%, -5 shows -5%, and 0 or none shows nothing. A value that is not a number shows nothing.

The team table's columns are: 'Team', 'Throughput', 'Remaining', 'Predicted', 'Trending', 'Δ'. Teams go by latest `completion.mean` first and teams with none last. Teams with equal dates are compared by a test that gives only 'after' or 'equal', so their order depends on the browser's sort (as the original does).

A team with a positive completion and a deviation of 0 or more has a normal row: name, throughput, its adjustment, remaining stories (`totalStories`), predicted stories, its adjustment, date and '±<days>d', days being `completion.deviation` over 86400000, to 1 decimal. Throughput and predicted cells are editable.
A normal team with a problem by the target date has its date marked with a warning 'The predicted finish date for this team is later than the target date.'.
A team with `completed` true shows a check with the text 'Team completed the work', throughput, stories, '-', the date and '-'. It has no editors.

A team with `ignore` true and no forecast shows only its name, stories and predicted stories, with the row title 'Some teams were ignored. Only completed stories of these teams are shown in the chart'.
Any other team has a warning 'Prediction Problem: <predictionProblem, or ?>' beside its name, in the date cell and in the deviation cell. Its throughput and predicted cells stay editable.

With at least one team, the last row is 'All Teams': the sum of `throughput`, of `totalStories`, and of `predictedStories` of teams not completed; the latest completion with its deviation (none when that team is completed). When any team has `predictionProblem` the row instead has a warning 'Prediction Problem: <first problem>' beside the name and in the last two cells. It cannot be selected.

A mouse press on a team's row selects it: the row is marked as the current one, with the tooltip 'The team currently displayed on the chart', and the chart shows that team's `teamCharts` entry, when there is one. A press elsewhere in the gadget clears the selection and returns to the overall chart. A selection survives a Refresh.

A team's chart is stretched to the overall chart's time range: an earlier first point with count 0 is added, and a later last point repeating the last counts. A team with no series gets one empty `done` series. The Y axis uses the overall final total, so team and overall charts share a scale.

Editing an adjustment: focus in an editor marks the column as focused. On blur or Enter the value is taken as a whole number (not a number gives 0; empty gives none). When it differs from the stored value, the team's entry is written to the `adjustments` preference, the editor shows the value and the simulation runs again. An unchanged value does nothing.
An adjustment editor is a number field with minimum -100, step 5, placeholder 0, with a '%' after it. Its starting value is the team's applied adjustment from the answer.
Tab and Shift+Tab in an adjustment editor move to the next or previous editor in the table, selecting that row's team when it differs. Past the first or last editor nothing happens.
'Refresh' runs the simulation again, showing a small spinner next to it. A second click while one runs is ignored. It does nothing before a good meta answer.

'Trace' shows or hides a read-only text box with the answer's `trace`. The text is filled only while the box is shown. While the user drags to resize the box the gadget refits at most every 200 ms, and once on release.

The gadget refits its frame to the page's scroll height after a change of the error, a result, a popup, or an attribute editor's resize, 50 ms after a simulation. On a window resize, 500 ms after the last event, it refits unless it refitted in the last second.

The CFD gadget's form has, in order: error list; 'Scope Structure'*; 'Training Structure'*; 'Training Period'*; 'Estimation Level'*; 'Scope Level'*; 'Team Attribute'*; 'Target Date'; then a heading 'Advanced Options'; 'When Added?'*; 'When Work Started?'*; 'When Completed?'*; 'Ignore threshold'. (* required.) It is sent to `GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate` by the framework, the field names being those parameters.
'Training Period' offers: 'All Time' (-1, selected by default), '1 Week' (7), '2 Weeks' (14), '3 Weeks' (21), '4 Weeks' (28), '6 Weeks' (42), '8 Weeks' (56).

'Estimation Level' and 'Scope Level' are multi-selects, placeholder 'Select one or more issue types', filled from Jira's `GET /rest/api/2/issuetype`. In an unconfigured gadget with nothing chosen, the first preselects types whose name has the word 'epic' and the second types with the word 'story', or starting with 'task', ignoring case.

Attribute fields are text areas holding the JSON spec with the attribute editor over them, expecting format `text` for 'Team Attribute' and `time` for the others. The attribute editor uses a standalone copy of the widget's attribute registry, with Jira's fields.
'Target Date' is a date picker in the format `yy-mm-dd`, placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD'. It is optional.
'Ignore threshold' is a number field from 0 to 100, placeholder 'Enter percents'. It is optional.

The chart is a stacked area chart, 400 high: `done` at the bottom, then `inProgress`, then `todo`, with no transition, built-in legend or tooltip. Time points are the X axis, from first to last, at most 5 ticks as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Y runs from 0 to the rounded final total times 1.1, at most 5 whole-number ticks. Negative counts draw as 0.
A legend above the chart lists 'TODO', 'IN PROGRESS' and 'DONE', in that order, for the series present. Hovering an entry focuses its series; leaving it reverts.
Each weekend's start (Saturday 00:00) and end (Monday 00:00), local time, inside the chart's time range, is a vertical grid line. A range with one point or none has none.

A 'Today' line is drawn at the present time, and a 'Target' line at the target date, each only inside the time range. Their labels sit centered on the line when both sides have room, else on the side with room, else are left out; other lines count as obstacles, and so do the chart's edges.

Each team with a positive completion date in the range has a short marker on the time axis, labelled with the team's name. Labels that would overlap go on higher rows, joined to their marker by a line. A line marks the latest completion among all teams; it is drawn even outside the range.

Hovering a team marker marks its row in the table and shows a popup: the team, 'Trending Date' (`YYYY-MM-DD`), 'Remaining Stories' and 'Predicted Stories' (empty for 0). The popup appears after 300 ms, or at once when another is open, and goes 300 ms after leaving. Leaving also clears the row mark.

The <product> Board page is decorated as a general Jira page, titled '<product>', with `wi-structure-link` as the current top menu section. Top down: the hidden issue operation links; a header area labelled '<product> toolbar' with the toolbar's collapse toggle and the toolbar's place; and the widget's place, labelled '<product> widget'. Jira's footer and feedback link are hidden, the page itself does not scroll vertically, and its minimum width is 1000 px.

Issue operation links must come before the widget in the page: Jira's issue shortcuts act on the first link with a given style class, so a cached row menu placed earlier would fire a link for the wrong issue. The same order holds on the project panel and the external gadget page.

The board's widget fills the window, has at least 6 rows, keeps its footer at the bottom and shows issue details, and the structure info dialog is available. The initial view (`view` when accessible, see `ww-structure`) and current structure are passed only when the server gives them. When the widget cannot be created the error is logged, in debug mode (`#debug` in the URL) also shown by an alert, and the page stays empty.
When the server says so (`structure.feature.createIssueAddsToBoardStructure`), the board's widget takes over Jira's Create Issue link, so that a created issue goes into the open structure.

The hidden operation links give one link per operation of `ww-structure`, with the operation's id, style class and URL, the URL still holding the placeholder `{0}` for the issue id; the grid opens them for a row. Hidden values next to them hold Jira's 'thanks' messages for updated, transitioned, assigned, commented, worklogged, voted, watched, moved, linked, cloned, labelled, deleted and attached issues, read from Jira's `navigator.results.thanks.*` keys, for the messages shown after an action.

The 'not permitted' page has the browser title 'Operation Not Permitted - <product>', the heading 'Operation Not Permitted' and a message of one sentence that the app did not permit the operation, probably for lack of permissions (the original's mention of the licence is left out, SPEC.md section 1.1). Its 'not ready' form has the title and heading '<product> Isn't Ready' and the text of `ww-structure`'s not-ready claim. There are no buttons.

The plain error page has Jira's word for error as title and heading, the section `wi-structure-link`, the note 'The requested operation was not successful. Sorry about that! Error messages, if any, are given below.', one list entry per error message (HTML-encoded), a 'Back' link to the return URL when there is one, and for an anonymous user Jira's login link `/login.jsp?os_destination=<this page, encoded>`.
The `success` view of `StructureAdmin!setProjects` and `StructureAdmin!setAppPermission` is an empty page: nothing is rendered in it.

`/secure/StructureSearchData.jspa` gives a bare page with three hidden JSON blocks: fields, functions and reserved words (see `ww-structure`). The JQL autocompletion of the widget and the gadget's form reads those.

The process status page is decorated as a general Jira page titled '<process name> - <product> Process Status', section `wi-structure-link`. It shows the process name as heading; 'Process Status'; 'Status:' with the state ('Pending', 'Running' or 'Finished'); the activity; '<n>% complete' when 0 to 100 is known; a progress bar; and one button per entry the process offers.

While the process is not finished, the page asks `GET /rest/structure/2.0/process/<id>/info` 3000 ms after load and 3000 ms after each answer. It stops at `status` 2. A page rendered for a finished process makes no request.

From the answer the page refreshes the name, status text, activity and percent text (each empty when missing). `percentComplete` from 0 to 100 sets and shows the progress bar; other values make it indeterminate. All buttons are rebuilt from `buttons`, each a link with `caption` and `url`.
A failed status request shows, as activity, 'Cannot update process status. Please try reloading this page or check Jira logs for details. (<error>)', clears the buttons and stops polling.

A process's cancel button is a link to a script action: after confirmation it sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/process/<id>/cancel`, JSON body `{}`, once, and treats the answer as a status answer. The question is 'Are you sure you want to cancel this process?', or the message whose key and parameters the button gives (a restore uses `sw.admin.restore.process.abort-confirm`). A finished or cancelled process ignores it; a failure is not shown.

The external gadget page (`/secure/StructureExternalGadget.jspa`) is titled '<product>'. Jira's header, footer and announcement banner are hidden, as is the widget's head, and the page has no vertical scroll. Links open in a new tab by default. Below the hidden operation links, the widget's place is labelled '<product> widget'. Jira's keyboard shortcuts are disabled on it.

URL parameters of the external gadget page: `gadgetid` (kept as the gadget's id), `readonly` (`true` forces the widget read-only), `view` (number, see the claim on saving), `filter` (`none`, `text`, `jql`, `sjql` or `saved`), `query` (filter text), `filterid` (number). `s` and `forcelogin` are as in `ww-structure`.

The page marks itself as the `gadget` page in `macro` mode. The widget fills the window, has at least 2 rows and shows no issue details. A filter from the URL becomes a transformation by the rule of `gadget-bare` (for `saved`, the JQL `filter="<id>"`), added to the panel. Widget failures are logged, and in debug mode also shown by an alert. The widget is observed by `visibility-observer`.
The external page's footer has the view links of `gadget-bare`, with 'Save' allowed only when the current view's id equals the URL's `view`, the view is writable and login is not offered.
When login is offered (anonymous viewer), the footer starts with a 'Login' link that opens in the same frame the current URL plus `forcelogin=true`.

The external gadget's unavailable page hides the same Jira parts and may scroll. Its heading is Jira's word for error when there are error messages, else 'Unavailable'. Its message, the first that applies: the 'not successful' note with each error; '<product> plugin is not available to the current user. Contact the administrator to change the setting.'; 'The selected structure has been deleted. Macro configuration is no longer correct.'; 'Current user has no permission to view the selected structure. Ask the owner to add such permission.'.
The external gadget's `login` and `gadgetlogin` outcomes show whatever the page's login renderer gives, as is, with no wrapper and no escaping.

The sync type chooser used by the sync pages shows the given 'none' message when no sync types exist. Otherwise it shows a label, a select of types (value the complete module key, text the type's label, the current `synctype` selected), a description that follows the selected type, an error under it for `synctype`, the submit button with the given text, and, when asked, 'Cancel' to the return URL. It posts `create=true` and `atl_token`.

The user picker field on the structure edit and cache-clearing forms is a text field with Jira's user autocomplete, single value, an icon link with the tooltip of Jira's `user.picker.select.user`, and Jira's help text. The link opens Jira's `/secure/popups/UserPickerBrowser.jspa?multiSelect=false&decorator=popup&element=<field name>&triggerEvent=customUserSelected` in a window 800 by 750; a chosen user is put in the field.

The wiki editor on the structure edit and help edit forms is Jira's wiki field: a text area with the given name holding the text, a rich text editor with the rendered content, and Jira's save option bar. The rendering is by `atlassian-wiki-renderer`. It needs Jira's preview button in the page, kept hidden.

On the Agile synchronizer's form, a second select's options follow a first one's value: only options mapped to the chosen value stay, except those marked to be always kept. With a multiple choice only options mapped to all chosen values stay; with no choice none. The second select's value is kept when still there. It updates at once on load and on each change or key press, and tells the page it changed.

On the sub-tasks synchronizer's form the multi-choice field is a box of checkboxes kept in a hidden field as ids joined by commas. Starting with no value all are checked unless told otherwise. The buttons 'All' and 'None' check and clear all, unless hidden. Names are HTML-encoded unless told otherwise.

The JQL field on the forms of `filter-jql`, `inserter-jql` and `effector-attribute-to-field` is a two-row text area named `jql`, with the given label and placeholder, a status icon, and an error under it for `jql`. When the JQL helper is loaded it adds Jira's autocompletion and live validation with the status icon, opens up the dialog so the suggestions are visible, and takes the focus when told to.

The forms of `extender-links` and `grouper-links` have 'Link Type': a select named `linkTypeId` of the visible link types, then a group 'Hidden Types' when any are hidden, with an error under it for `linkTypeId`. Then 'Link Direction': 'parent issue', a select named `direction`, 'sub-issue'. The direction's options `outward`, `inward` and `any` take their text from the chosen type's labels, at once and on each change of type.

The summary of a links generator is the given message with the link type name and direction name when both parameters are stored, else the given 'none' message with the 'none specified' text. `extender-links` does the same.
The field's `view` shows its value as it is, and nothing for no value. As the value is always empty (see the module's claims), the screen is empty.

The searcher's `search` screen is the value, unescaped, followed by Jira's standard custom control footer; `view` is the value followed by Jira's searcher footer; `label` is the value. Those are empty, so only Jira's footers show.

The workflow form's row 'Structure' has the radios (name `structureType`) 'The default structure of the issue's project' (`default`), 'Manually selected:' (`manual`) with a select named `structureId`, and 'The one that contains the issue' (`containing`) with the note 'If the issue is contained in 2 or more structures, the transition will be blocked.'. The stored value is checked. The select is enabled only with 'Manually selected:' checked.

An option of the workflow form's select shows the structure's abbreviated name; a name shared by other structures also shows ' [<id>]' or ' [<id>, <owner text>]'. A stored id that is not in the list adds a selected option '? [<id>]'.

When the stored value is `containing`, that radio is absent. In its place is the warning 'It is no longer possible to automatically pick the structure that contains the issue. Please choose another option.', and no radio is checked.

The form's row 'S-JQL Query' has a text area named `queryString` with two rows, a link to the plugin's S-JQL documentation (title 'Syntax Help', opening in a new tab; the implementer's own link), and the note 'The issue must match this query to pass the transition.'.

The form has 'Query examples:' with a select that starts on 'pick an example' (empty value): under the query for a condition, under 'Validator Message' for a validator. Choosing an example puts its query into the query field and, on a validator, its text into 'Validator Message'. Editing the query by hand puts the select back on 'pick an example'.

The form's row is labelled 'If the Issue Is Not Added to the Structure', or 'If the Issue Is Not Added to Any Structure' while 'containing' is chosen. Its radios (name `allowUnstructured`): 'Allow transition' (`true`), 'Block transition' (`false`).

The form's row 'Run as User' has the radios (name `runAsLead`) 'Project lead' (`true`), 'Specific user:' (`false`) with a text field named `runAsUserName` (note 'Please enter a username.'), enabled only with 'Specific user:' checked, and the warning 'All operations will be performed on behalf of the specified user.'.
The form shows an error box below the field for each of `structureId`, `structureType`, `queryString` and `runAsUserName` when the factory reports one.

The condition's summary in Jira's workflow editor always starts with 'Issue must match the <product> query.' and lists the same facts as the validator's, and shows the errors of `structureType`, `structureId`, `queryString` and `runAsUserName`, each below its fact. An unknown structure type, or a `manual` one with no readable structure, shows '?'. Unstructured's label follows `containing` as on the form.

The validator's form also has the row 'Validator Message': a text field named `queryDesc` with the note 'Optional field. Users will see this message when the issue does not match the query.'. All else is as on the form of `structure-workflow-condition`.
